question.:question/problem:
A pork leg is taken out of the oven with a temperature of ${149}^{∘}C,$ and placed in a room that maintains a temperature of ${20}^{∘}C$, and its temperature begins to decrease. After $4$ minutes, the  temperature of the pork leg is ${132}^{∘}C.$ To the nearest minute, how long does it take for the pork leg to have a temperature of ${101}^{∘}C?$ 

*Hint: You may assume that the temperature reading $T(t)$ of the pork leg decreases at a rate that obeys Newton's law of cooling, where $T$ is measured in degrees Celsius and $t>0$ is the time, in minutes, since the pork leg was transferred into the ${20}^{∘}C$ room.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Newton's law of cooling states that the rate at which the temperature $T(t)$ of a body changes is proportional to the difference between its temperature and its surroundings. Therefore, we have the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-{T}_{S}),
$$

where ${T}_{S}$ is the temperature of the surroundings, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, ${T}_{S}={20}^{∘}\text{C},$ and we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-20).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-20} & =-k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-20} & =-k\int dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-20| & =-kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-20>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-20 & ={e}^{-kt+C} \\ T-20 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-kt} \\ T-20 & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ T & =20+K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial temperature of the pork leg was ${149}^{∘}C.$ So, we apply the initial condition $T(0)=149,$ and solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}149 & =20+K{e}^{0} \\ 149 & =20+K \\ K & =129\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $T(t):$

$$
T(t)=20+129{e}^{-kt}
$$

We're also told that, after $4$ minutes, the temperature of the pork leg is ${132}^{∘}C.$ So, applying the condition $T(4)=132,$ we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}132 & =20+129{e}^{-4k} \\ 112 & =129{e}^{-4k} \\ \frac{112}{129} & ={e}^{-4k} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{112}{129}\right) & =-4k \\ k & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{112}{129}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the pork leg has a temperature of ${101}^{∘}C.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T({t}_{1}) & =101 \\ 20+129{e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =101 \\ 129{e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =81 \\ {e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =\frac{27}{43} \\ -k{t}_{1} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{27}{43}\right) \\ {t}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{27}{43}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in our value for $k,$ we conclude that the pork leg will have a temperature of ${101}^{∘}C$ after

$$
{t}_{1}=\frac{-\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{27}{43}\right)}{-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{112}{129}\right)}≈13\,\text{min},
$$

rounded to the nearest minute.

generation.domain: T(t)>ambient; positive rate; t>=0; observations strictly cooling
